text:
Sam K: FYI CI flagged a perf regression on PR #14723 — microbench p99 for the kv_batcher path is +8.3% vs main, threshold failed. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood/example/14723/artifacts :eyes:
Jess W: Ugh, do we have the commit range? which change touched the kernel selector / batching heuristics?
Sam K: Range is main..feature/pr-14723, culprit looks like commit abc1234 (kernel: autoselect heuristic + batching window tweak). Diff: https://git.redwood/commit/abc1234
Marta P: Running a local bisect now. quick note: CI profile shows longer batch wait times and more kv cache churn.
ci-bot: perf-alert: pr-14723 | microbench/kv_batcher | p99 +8.3% | test=bench_kv_batcher | thresholds.json diff attached
Marta P: Bisect result: points to abc1234 — the change set is two parts: (1) kernel autoselect changed preference rules, (2) batch_timer increased from 4ms -> 6ms when seq_len_predict > 128.
Jess W: Increasing timer could increase KV eviction pressure (longer request aggregation -> larger KV working sets). Did you capture hit-rate?
Marta P: Yep. Before: kv_hitrate ~87%. After (on bisect candidate): kv_hitrate ~71%. Also seeing mutex hotspot in kernel_registry during kernel selection. Quick profile snippet:
```
# flame top (samples)
kernel_registry::select_kernel 42 (42.3%)
kv_cache::evict_if_needed 12 (12.1%)
batcher::wait_for_batch 9 (9.4%)
```
Sam K: Interesting — so kernel autoselect entering a more expensive path while batches hold onto KV entries. Could be combo effect.
Liam R: Short-term mitigations: (A) revert the batching window bump, or (B) tweak autoselect to avoid switching to the new kernel for short sequences. Revert is fastest for rollout.
Jess W: Can we try a minimal patch that keeps the timer at 4ms but keeps the autoselect changes? that would isolate which piece causes the regression.
Marta P: On it. Patching locally to force batch_timer=4ms and re-run microbench. Command:
```
./scripts/run_microbench --bench bench_kv_batcher --repeats 5 --env BATCH_TIMER_MS=4
```
Sam K: Results from Marta's run with BATCH_TIMER_MS=4ms (5 runs): p99 delta = +0.6% (within noise). kv_hitrate restored to ~86%. Looks like batch_timer change is the primary driver.
Liam R: Great — that suggests we should revert the timer change in this PR and follow up with a measured rollout of autoselect changes behind a feature flag.
Sam K: I'll open a hotfix revert PR now and mark current PR as blocked for rollout until we have a proper plan. Opening: https://git.redwood/pr/14724-revert-batch-timer
Jess W: Also add a perf unit test that asserts kv_hitrate >= 80% for the canonical seq_len distribution so we catch this earlier.
Marta P: Agreed. I'll add a small regression test and a perf golden for kv hitrate.
ci-bot: note: re-run queued for pr-14724 (hotfix revert).
Sam K: Thanks all — marking as rollout-blocker and adding notes to the PR. :white_check_mark:
